identity.title: ALMA Spectroscopic Survey in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field: CO Luminosity Functions and the Evolution of the Cosmic Density of Molecular Gas

paper_type_evidence.quote: we use ASPECS, the ALMA Spectroscopic Survey in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field (UDF) in band 3 and band 6, to place blind constraints on the CO luminosity function

distance_source.value: line identification with optical/near-IR spectroscopic, grism or photometric redshifts

question.value: What are the blind CO luminosity functions and the evolution of the cosmic molecular gas density rho(H2) up to z~4.5, from ALMA band 3 and 6 scans of the UDF?

evidence.quote: place blind constraints on the CO luminosity function and the evolution of the cosmic molecular gas density as a function of redshift up to $z\sim 4.5$
two frequency scans at 3mm (band 3) and 1mm (band 6) obtained with ALMA in the UDF
The 3mm scan covers the 84-115 GHz range with a single spatial pointing.
The 1mm scan encompasses the frequency window 212-272 GHz.

lines_targeted.transition: J=1-0 through 6-5 (CO(2-1) to CO(4-3) used in luminosity functions)

evidence.quote: The synthesized beams are $\sim 3.5''\times 2.0''$ at 3mm and $\sim 1.5''\times 1.0''$ at 1mm.

sensitivity.value: 0.15 mJy/beam per 20 MHz channel (3mm); ~0.5 mJy/beam per 30 MHz channel (1mm)

evidence.quote: The typical RMS noise is 0.15 mJy beam$^{-1}$ per 20 MHz channel.
The typical depth of the data is $\sim 0.5$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ per 30 MHz channel.

provided.value: Redshifts (slit spectroscopy, 3D-HST grism, photometric) for line identification and stacking

evidence.quote: Optical spectroscopy (cite: lefevre05; coe06; skelton14; morris15) is considered secure

what.value: Blind CO line catalog (10 3mm and 11 1mm candidates) with line fluxes, widths, frequencies

evidence.quote: We first concentrated on the “blind” CO detections presented in Paper I (Tab. 2)

what.value: CO excitation ratios r_J1 = 0.76, 0.42, 0.23 for J=2,3,5
1mm continuum source flux densities used for dust-based ISM masses

evidence.quote: for each 1mm continuum source (see the companion paper (cite: aravena16a)), the ISM mass is computed

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Semi-analytical model and empirical CO luminosity function predictions (Lagos+12, Popping+16, Vallini+16) compared with the measurements

evidence.quote: we include the predictions based on semi-analytical models by (cite: lagos12) and (cite: popping16) and on empirical IR luminosity function of *Herschel* sources by (cite: vallini16)

what.value: Observations, data reduction and imaging are described in Paper I

evidence.quote: Details on the observations and data reduction are presented in Paper I, but the relevant information is briefly summarized here.
as described in Sec. 3.1.1 of Paper I
These are derived following (cite: scoville14).
Following (cite: daddi10a), we thus assume $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 3.6$

unstated_but_needed: Calibration and imaging settings (all in Paper I)
ALMA project codes and observing dates
Exact floating-average channel widths and S/N thresholds of the blind search
Luminosity bin edges and mapping to the plotted points
Gamma_RJ values used for the dust masses
Complete catalog of mock line parameters for completeness

analysis_steps.goal: Blind line search and line identification

method.value: Floating average of channels in 50-300 km/s bins, S/N peak selection; identification via multiple lines, absence of counterparts, and optical/NIR redshifts

evidence.quote: we perform a floating average of consecutive frequency channels in bins of $\sim$50–300 km s$^{-1}$ in the imaged cubes.
The final catalogue consists of 10 line candidates from the 3mm cube, and 11 from the 1mm cube.

fitting.value: Gaussian fit to candidate spectra for flux, width, frequency

evidence.quote: We use a Gaussian fit of the candidate spectra to estimate the line flux, width, and frequency

validation.value: Bootstrap of 1000 redshift draws proportional to comoving volume over possible line identifications

evidence.quote: We then run 1000 extractions of the redshift values picked from their probability distributions

method.value: Fidelity from negative peaks; completeness from 2500 injected mock point-source lines

evidence.quote: This is obtained by creating a sample of 2500 mock lines (as point sources)
the fidelity at a given S/N is defined as $(N_{\rm pos}-N_{\rm neg})/N_{\rm pos}$

validation.value: Flux boosting argued negligible due to S/N>5

evidence.quote: make the impact of flux boosting negligible in our analysis

analysis_steps.goal: Line luminosity and CO luminosity functions

method.value: L' from Solomon+97 formula; Phi = (1/V) sum Fid/C in 1-dex bins; Gehrels Poisson errors

evidence.quote: The uncertainties on $\Phi(\log L_i)$ are set by the Poissonian errors on $N_i$, according to (cite: gehrels86)

validation.value: Comparison with Lagos+12, Popping+16, Vallini+16 predictions and HDF-N

evidence.quote: we include the predictions based on semi-analytical models by (cite: lagos12) and (cite: popping16) and on empirical IR luminosity function of *Herschel* sources by (cite: vallini16), as well as the constraints obtained by the earlier study of the HDF–N

method.value: log L'(1-0) = log L'(J) - log r_J1 with Daddi+15 template

evidence.quote: $$\log L_{\rm CO(1-0)}'=\log L_{\rm CO(J-[J-1])}'-\log r_{\rm J1}$$
yielding $r_{41}$=$0.31\pm0.06$, where we conservatively assume a 20% uncertainty

validation.value: Robustness checked with the CO(2-1) bin where excitation corrections are small

evidence.quote: This result is robust against CO excitation uncertainties: For example, it is already apparent in the $\langle z\rangle =1.43$ bin, where we covered the CO(2-1) line in our 3mm cube

method.value: M_H2 = alpha_CO L'(1-0); rho(H2) = (1/V) sum M P / C

evidence.quote: $$M_{\rm H2}=\alpha_{\rm CO} \, L_{\rm CO(1-0)}'$$

assumptions.value: alpha_CO = 3.6 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1 for all sources

evidence.quote: we thus assume $\alpha_{\rm CO} = 3.6$ M$_\odot$ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$ for all the sources in our sample

validation.value: Not extrapolated beyond the observed luminosity range

evidence.quote: we do not attempt to correct for undetected galaxies in lower luminosity bins given the large uncertainties in the individual luminosity bins and the unknown intrinsic shape of the CO luminosity function.

method.value: Scoville+14 recipe on 1mm continuum sources detected to S/N=3, summed per redshift bin

evidence.quote: We include here all the sources detected down to S/N=3 in the 1mm continuum.
$\Gamma_0=0.71$ is the tuning value obtained at low-$z$
The dust temperature (implicit in the definition of $\Gamma_{\rm RJ}$), is set to 25 K.
we compare the constraints on $\rho$(H$_2$) inferred from CO with those on $\rho$(ISM) derived from the dust continuum in our observations of the UDF.
The code for the blind search of line candidates is publicly available at http://www.mpia.de/homes/decarli/ASPECS/findclumps.cl.

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of CO luminosity recovered (lower bound)

evidence.quote: we recover a large part ($>$50%) of the total CO luminosity per comoving volume

results_numeric.quantity: Evolution of cosmic H2 density z~2 vs z=0

evidence.quote: The global amount of molecular gas stored in galaxies at the peak epoch of galaxy assembly is 3–10 times larger than at the present day.
Our analysis is 50% complete down to line luminosities of $(4-6) \times 10^9$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$ at 3mm for any J$>$1

results_numeric.quantity: Cosmic variance fractional uncertainty at z~2.5

evidence.quote: the fractional uncertainty in the number counts due to cosmic variance is $\sim 20$% ($\sim 60$% if we include Poissonian fluctuations)

findings_qualitative.value: CO luminosity function knee shifts to higher luminosities from z~0 to z~2, with excess of bright sources relative to models at z>1, while 1mm shows low CO excitation

evidence.quote: Our measurements reveal that the knee of the CO(1-0) luminosity function shifts toward higher luminosities as we move from $z\approx 0$

findings_qualitative.value: Dust-based densities are consistent with CO-based at z<2 but lower at z>2

evidence.quote: discrepancies are found at $z>2$, where $\rho$(H$_2$) estimates based on CO tend to be larger than $\rho$(ISM) estimates based on dust

claims.hypothesis: Does the CO luminosity function evolve from z~0 to z~2?
claims.experiment: Blind CO LFs in redshift bins, converted to CO(1-0)
claims.result: Knee shifts to higher luminosities; excess of bright sources at z>1 vs models
claims.finding: More CO-luminous, gas-rich galaxies at z~2 than models predict

evidence.quote: at $z>1$ they suggest an excess of CO–luminous sources, compared to the current models

claims.hypothesis: How does rho(H2) evolve with redshift?
claims.experiment: Sum of completeness- and fidelity-corrected H2 masses per bin
claims.result: 3-10x higher at z~2 than z=0, possible decline at z>3
claims.finding: Cosmic gas density follows the SFR density evolution partly

evidence.quote: shows a factor 3–10 drop from $z \sim 2$ to $z \sim 0$ (with significant error bars), and possibly a decline at $z>3$

claims.hypothesis: Do dust-based and CO-based gas densities agree?
claims.result: Roughly consistent at z<2, dust lower at z>2
claims.finding: Possible causes are dust temperature/opacity or alpha_CO

evidence.quote: even applying the more recent calibration would not be sufficient to significantly mitigate the discrepancy

why_this_method.value: Blank-field scan avoids pre-selection bias and gives a well-defined volume

evidence.quote: By focusing on a blank field, we avoid the biases due to pre-selection of sources.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Stack of 36 spectroscopic-redshift galaxies excluded due to only ~2-sigma detections

evidence.quote: we opt not to include them in the remainder of the analysis

limitations_admitted.value: rho(H2) is a lower limit as faint end not recovered; Poisson errors and cosmic variance large

evidence.quote: our constraints on $\rho$(H$_2$) are actually lower limits, in the sense that they do not recover the full extent of the luminosity function

referee_caveats_inferred: Single small field with strong cosmic variance
Ambiguous line identifications for 11 of 21 lines handled statistically
Fixed alpha_CO and excitation template drive rho(H2)
